questions.title: Single Loop Iteration Count
questions.description:
A loop runs "for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) work();". Return how many times the body runs. Do not simulate the loop — answer from the formula, n can be huge. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long single_loop_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Nested Pair Iteration Count
questions.description:
A loop pair runs "for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) work();". The body runs exactly once per ordered pair (j, i) with 0 <= j < i < n — that is n * (n - 1) / 2 times. Do not simulate; n can be large. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long nested_pair_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the body-execution count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Halving Loop Steps
questions.description:
A loop runs "while (n > 1) n /= 2;". Return how many times the body runs. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int halving_steps(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of halving steps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Gauss Loop Sum
questions.description:
A loop runs "for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) sum += i;" and accumulates 1 + 2 + ... + n. Return that total without simulating the loop. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long loop_sum(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000000

questions.title: Doubling Steps to Limit
questions.description:
A loop runs "while (x < 1000000) x *= 2;" starting from x = start. Return how many times the body runs. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int doubling_steps(int start)

Input Format:
One line with the starting value.

Output Format:
One line with the number of doubling steps.

Constraints:
1 <= start <= 1000000

questions.title: Skip Loop Count
questions.description:
A loop runs "for (int i = 0; i < n; i += 3) work();" — it advances by 3 each step. Return how many times the body runs. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int skip_loop_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count (this is ceil(n / 3)).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Pairwise Module Tests
questions.description:
A QA team must test every unordered pair of n modules exactly once. Return the number of test pairs, n * (n - 1) / 2. Do not simulate; n can be large. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long pair_tests(int n)

Input Format:
One line with the module count.

Output Format:
One line with the number of unordered pairs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Antivirus Sweep Count
questions.description:
An antivirus sweeps a quarantined folder once per minute, removing half of the infected files each sweep (rounded down). Sweep after sweep continues while more than one infected file remains. Return how many sweeps happen for n infected files. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int sweep_count(int n)

It must answer the same question as the loop "while (n > 1) n /= 2;" — how many halvings until n reaches 1.

Input Format:
One line with the infected-file count.

Output Format:
One line with the number of sweeps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bulk Batcher Batches
questions.description:
A warehouse packs items into boxes of 3; the last box may hold fewer than 3 items. Return how many boxes are needed for n items — that is ceil(n / 3). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int batch_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with the item count.

Output Format:
One line with the box count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Double Pass Inventory Scan
questions.description:
A warehouse robot scans every one of n shelves once for stock-taking and once again for labelling — two independent linear passes, so the work is exactly 2 * n shelf visits. Return the visit count; answer from the model, n can be huge. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long double_scan(int n)

This models a Theta(n) algorithm whose constant factor is 2.

Input Format:
One line with the shelf count.

Output Format:
One line with the total shelf visits.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Loop Census
questions.description:
An analysis tool reports two counts for input size n: the iterations of one simple loop over n items, and the body executions of the triangular nesting "for i in 0..n-1, for j in 0..i-1". Fill both out-parameters with closed-form values — loops are not allowed in your answer. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void loop_census(int n, long long &single, long long &pairs)

single gets n; pairs gets n * (n - 1) / 2.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with single, then pairs, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Merge Pass Planner
questions.description:
A merge-sort planner needs the number of merge levels for n items: start with a run size of 1 and keep doubling it until it reaches n — count the doublings. Use a while loop. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int merge_passes(int n)

For n = 1 the answer is 0.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of doublings (ceil of log2 of n).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Big-O Class Identifier
questions.description:
A teaching tool maps snippet IDs to complexity ranks. The snippets are:
1 → O(n log n), 2 → O(1), 3 → O(n^2), 4 → O(log n), 5 → O(n), 6 → O(2^n).
Rank them from fastest to slowest: O(1) is rank 1, O(log n) rank 2, O(n) rank 3, O(n log n) rank 4, O(n^2) rank 5, O(2^n) rank 6. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int big_o_class(int id)

It must return the rank (1-6) of the snippet with the given id. Use an if-chain — no switch, no containers.

Input Format:
One line with the snippet id (1-6).

Output Format:
One line with the complexity rank.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 6

questions.title: Front and Back Scan Compare
questions.description:
A lost-luggage desk can scan n lockers from the front or from the back. A specific item sits at position pos (1-indexed). Scanning from the front inspects pos lockers; scanning from the back inspects n - pos + 1 lockers. Fill both out-parameters — arithmetic only, no loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void scan_compare(int n, int pos, int &front, int &back)

Input Format:
One line with n and pos.

Output Format:
One line with front, then back, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= pos <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Memory Footprint Model
questions.description:
An int occupies 4 bytes. A flat int array of n elements uses 4 * n bytes; an n x n int matrix uses 4 * n * n bytes. Fill both out-parameters — arithmetic only, no loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void space_bytes(int n, long long &flat, long long &grid)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with flat, then grid, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Cubic Triple Count
questions.description:
A brute-force triple checker runs "for i in 1..n, for j in i+1..n, for k in j+1..n" — its body executes once per combination of three distinct indices, i.e. C(n, 3) = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6 times. Return that count with a closed-form formula — no loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long triple_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the triple count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Divisor Sieve Workload
questions.description:
A number-theory sieve runs "for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) for (j = i; j <= n; j += i) mark(j);" — the inner body executes once for every multiple of every i, exactly sum over i of floor(n / i) times. Count those executions by running the actual double loop (n is small enough). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long sieve_work(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total body-execution count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20000

questions.title: Quadratic Crossover Finder
questions.description:
A profiler wants the input size where an O(n^2) routine overtakes an O(n) routine with overhead: find the smallest n >= 1 such that n * n > slope * n + intercept. Solve it with a while loop that walks n upward from 1 — no sqrt, no pow. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int crossover_point(int slope, int intercept)

Input Format:
One line with slope and intercept.

Output Format:
One line with the smallest n where n * n > slope * n + intercept.

Constraints:
0 <= slope <= 1000, 0 <= intercept <= 100000

questions.title: Naive Fibonacci Call Count
questions.description:
The naive recursion calls(n) = 1 + calls(n - 1) + calls(n - 2) with calls(0) = calls(1) = 1 explodes exponentially — for n up to 30 you must NOT simulate it. Compute the count with an iterative Fibonacci-style walk instead (the count equals 2 * fib(n + 1) - 1 where fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fib_calls(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total number of calls the naive recursion makes.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Merge Work Estimator
questions.description:
A merge-sort cost model says: levels = the number of times you can double 1 until it reaches n (0 when n is 1), and work = n * levels element-moves across all merges. Fill both out-parameters with a while loop — no for loops, no pow, no logarithm calls. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void merge_model(int n, long long &levels, long long &work)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with levels, then work, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
